DocumentationNarrative.Body:
## A complete BI stack built by an agent
The AdventureWorks stack was fully designed and built by an agent using the public Meta and meta-bi command-line tools. Its starting inputs were a live `AdventureWorks2022` database and a short [business request](https://github.com/jimmy-zhao-tainio/meta-bi/blob/main/Demos/AdventureWorksBiStackDemo/BUSINESS-REQUIREMENTS.md) for sales trends, channel and product analysis, geography, salesperson quotas, and visible data-quality risks.
The agent made the architectural decisions that turn those inputs into a BI system. It selected sales order, sales line, and salesperson quota as separate fact grains; kept tax and freight at order grain; created shared date, product, geography, customer, channel, and salesperson dimensions; derived the Online/Store channel from source evidence; and declined to publish gross margin because AdventureWorks lacks complete historical cost coverage.
The implementation is preserved as models rather than summarized after the fact. Every generated workspace was created through its owning CLI. The demo's MetaMesh workspace names 27 participating workspaces, 29 operations, and 614 ordered executable steps covering discovery, model authoring, conversion, deployment, transformation import and binding, pipeline construction, execution, verification, and analytical deployment. The generated results are checked in alongside that construction record.
## What the agent built
Each product owns a concrete part of the resulting stack:
| Engineering concern | AdventureWorks result | Modeled capability | | --- | --- | --- | | Discover the live source | 6 schemas, 71 tables, 20 views, 744 fields, and 90 relationships | `meta-schema` extracts a reviewable `MetaSchema` source contract. | | Preserve source history | 71 Raw hubs, 90 links, 71 satellites, and 341 satellite attributes | `meta-datavault-raw` and `meta-convert` turn the source contract into `MetaRawDataVault`, then into 232 deployable `MetaSql` tables through an explicit implementation model. | | Establish business meaning | 14 Business hubs, 19 links, 14 satellites, stable business names, and the Online/Store derivation | `meta-datavault-business` authors `MetaBusinessDataVault` concepts separately from the source-shaped Raw layer. | | Fix analytical grain | 3 facts, 8 conformed dimensions, 10 warehouse measures, 40 dimension attributes, and 19 fact-to-dimension relationships | `meta-data-warehouse` authors `MetaDataWarehouse`; `meta-convert` projects it through an implementation model into an 11-table physical warehouse. | | Make transformations provable | 53 source-to-Raw, 47 Raw-to-Business, and 20 Business-to-warehouse transformations, each strictly bound | `meta-transform-script` models the T-SQL program; `meta-transform-binding`, `MetaSchema`, `MetaDataType`, and `MetaDataTypeConversion` prove its reads, writes, target shape, and type compatibility. | | Turn evidence into quality checks | 167 promoted checks covering orphan joins, multiplicity expansion, duplicate risk, and outer-join null expansion | `meta-data-quality` derives reviewable `MetaDataQuality` candidates and `meta-convert` emits executable quality SQL. | | Operate the load | 3 pipelines containing 120 transformation tasks, plus one inferred orchestration plan over the same 120 tasks | `meta-pipeline` executes and records work; `meta-orchestration` derives and governs runtime dependencies. | | Publish portable analytics | 11 analytical tables, 72 attributes, 11 base measures, 3 hierarchies, and 19 relationships | `meta-analytics` carries engine-neutral `MetaAnalytics`; `meta-convert` and `meta-tabular` produce and operate the Analysis Services model. | | Model the conversion itself | One requirement and 24 executable Analytics-to-Tabular transformations | `meta-weave` executes a `MetaWeave` correspondence whose WeaveScript projection is readable and editable modeled transformation. |
## Prerequisites
- the `meta` and `meta-bi` CLIs on `PATH`; - a local SQL Server instance with `AdventureWorks2022` restored; - permission to create the four demo-owned databases; - Analysis Services Tabular only when running the optional Tabular deployment and processing operations.
[`SOURCE-SETUP.md`](https://github.com/jimmy-zhao-tainio/meta-bi/blob/main/Demos/AdventureWorksBiStackDemo/SOURCE-SETUP.md) covers the source database. [`prepare-adventureworks-db.ps1`](https://github.com/jimmy-zhao-tainio/meta-bi/blob/main/Demos/AdventureWorksBiStackDemo/prepare-adventureworks-db.ps1) can download and restore the official backup on a local development machine.
## Environment
The examples below use the local default SQL Server instance:
```powershell $env:AW_SOURCE_SQL = "Server=.;Database=AdventureWorks2022;Integrated Security=true;TrustServerCertificate=true;Encrypt=false" $env:AW_ADMIN_SQL = "Server=.;Database=master;Integrated Security=true;TrustServerCertificate=true;Encrypt=false" $env:AW_RDV_SQL = "Server=.;Database=AdventureWorksRawVault;Integrated Security=true;TrustServerCertificate=true;Encrypt=false" $env:AW_BDV_SQL = "Server=.;Database=AdventureWorksBusinessVault;Integrated Security=true;TrustServerCertificate=true;Encrypt=false" $env:AW_DW_SQL = "Server=.;Database=AdventureWorksAnalytics;Integrated Security=true;TrustServerCertificate=true;Encrypt=false" $env:AW_PIPELINE_SQL = "Server=.;Database=AdventureWorksMetaPipeline;Integrated Security=true;TrustServerCertificate=true;Encrypt=false" ```
## Build the stack
Run from the mesh workspace:
```powershell cd AdventureWorksBiStackDemo.MetaMesh
meta-mesh run --operation validate-source meta-mesh run --operation sync-source-schema
meta-mesh run --operation create-raw-vault meta-mesh run --operation deploy-raw-vault meta-mesh run --operation create-source-raw-transforms meta-mesh run --operation create-source-raw-pipeline
meta-mesh run --operation create-business-vault meta-mesh run --operation deploy-business-vault meta-mesh run --operation create-raw-business-transforms meta-mesh run --operation create-raw-business-pipeline
meta-mesh run --operation create-dimensional-warehouse meta-mesh run --operation deploy-dimensional-warehouse meta-mesh run --operation create-business-warehouse-transforms meta-mesh run --operation create-business-warehouse-pipeline
meta-mesh run --operation create-orchestration meta-mesh run --operation deploy-pipeline-runtime meta-mesh run --operation create-data-quality meta-mesh run --operation deploy-data-quality meta-mesh run --operation create-analytics meta-mesh run --operation create-tabular ```
The three transform boundaries are strictly bound to modeled source and target schemas before their pipelines are authored. Orchestration is inferred from those pipeline tasks and binding effects.
## Run and verify
Execute the inferred graph across all three pipelines, then reconcile the result to the source:
```powershell meta-mesh run --operation run-etl meta-mesh run --operation verify-stack ```
For an inspected layer-by-layer run, use `load-raw-vault`, `load-business-vault`, and `load-dimensional-warehouse` instead of `run-etl`.
The verification operation checks Raw and Business Vault counts, warehouse fact grains, source-to-warehouse measures, deployed Data Quality results, and the latest task-level pipeline evidence. The expected static AdventureWorks result is 31,465 orders, 121,317 lines, 163 quota rows, and 167 promoted Data Quality checks with no findings.
## Tabular runtime
The MetaAnalytics and MetaTabular workspaces are complete without Analysis Services. The runtime operations target the local `.\TABULAR` instance and deploy the model as `AdventureWorksSales`:
```powershell meta-mesh run --operation deploy-tabular meta-mesh run --operation process-tabular ```
`deploy-tabular` replaces the target database and deploys metadata without processing. `process-tabular` performs the full refresh. `drop-tabular` removes the deployed database.
The deployment operation also grants the local `NT Service\MSOLAP$TABULAR` service account read access to `AdventureWorksAnalytics`. The verified deployment contains 11 tables, 72 columns, 11 measures, and 19 relationships and completes a full refresh on `.\TABULAR`. A direct model query returns Sales Amount `109846381.425`, Total Due `123216786.1159`, and Quota Amount `95714000`, matching the relational verification.
## Cleanup
```powershell meta-mesh run --operation cleanup ```
Cleanup drops `AdventureWorksRawVault`, `AdventureWorksBusinessVault`, `AdventureWorksAnalytics`, and `AdventureWorksMetaPipeline`, then removes transient pipeline execution evidence under `Runs\ops\RunArtifacts`. It keeps the checked-in modeled workspaces. It does not remove the source database or an external Tabular database.

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Conversions carry one workspace into the next part of the system. `meta-convert` covers the established paths: schema to Raw Data Vault; Raw and Business Data Vault to SQL; data warehouse to SQL; SQL and TransformScript in both directions; Data Quality to SQL; and MetaAnalytics to Tabular or Multidimensional models.
MetaWeave brings the conversion itself into a model. A `MetaWeave` workspace names the source and target contracts, the available directions, their requirements, and the transformations that populate target entities. Those transformations have a readable WeaveScript form and execute through MetaWeave's in-memory engine. The result of `meta-weave execute` is a new workspace in the selected XML, SQL, or C# representation.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Conversions

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
A BI build uses many workspaces and many CLI calls. MetaMesh turns that construction path into a workspace of its own: participating workspaces, executables, arguments, named operations, and ordered steps.
An operation can begin with source discovery, create the vault and warehouse models, convert them into database structures, deploy them, import and bind transforms, build pipelines, derive orchestration, execute the load, check the result, and publish an analytical model. Other operations can refresh one layer, deploy one target, or run one verification sequence.
`meta-mesh validate` resolves the declared workspaces and commands before execution. `meta-mesh run` then invokes each step in the recorded order. The mesh workspace keeps the construction process alongside the model workspaces and gives the system named entry points for build, deployment, execution, verification, and cleanup.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Building systems with MetaMesh

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
The model set follows the working parts of a BI system, from source structure through data stores and transforms to runtime and analytics.
#### Schemas and data types
Work can begin by extracting SQL Server into `MetaSchema`. The resulting workspace contains schemas, objects, fields, keys, and relationships that other models can reference. Other systems can provide the same contract through `MetaSchemaAdapter`. `MetaDataType` gives those fields shared type identities, and `MetaDataTypeConversion` carries the conversion rules used when source and target systems use different type systems.
#### Data Vault
From a source contract, the Raw Data Vault model captures hubs, links, satellites, business keys, and descriptive fields in `MetaRawDataVault`. Business integration is authored in `MetaBusinessDataVault`, including Business hubs, links, satellites, bridges, point-in-time structures, and their supporting relationships.
`MetaDataVaultImplementation` supplies schemas and names, SQL types, hashing policy, audit columns, defaults, and indexes. Conversion combines a vault workspace with that implementation workspace and produces the corresponding `MetaSql` database structure.
#### Data warehouse
Dimensional design begins with grain. `MetaDataWarehouse` carries facts, dimensions, attributes, measures, dimensional roles, table types, historization, and the relationships that connect them. `MetaDataWarehouseImplementation` applies schemas and naming, surrogate keys, slowly-changing-dimension columns, SQL types, defaults, and indexes when that design is converted into database tables.
#### Transforms
`MetaTransformScript` is a semantic model of supported T-SQL. It carries statements, queries, CTEs, row sources, expressions, functions, identifiers, ordering, and mutations as related model entities. SQL can be imported into that model, inspected and changed as workspace data, and emitted again as T-SQL.
Binding places those transforms against source and target `MetaSchema` workspaces. `MetaTransformBinding` resolves object and field references, derives input and output rowsets, records reads and writes, matches projected columns to target columns, and applies the selected `MetaDataTypeConversion` rules. The resulting binding workspace feeds data-quality discovery, pipeline execution, and orchestration analysis.
#### SQL databases
`MetaSql` carries the SQL Server database structure produced by the design and transform models, and it can also be extracted from SQL Server. `meta-sql deploy-plan` compares a MetaSql workspace with a live database and writes a `MetaSqlDeployManifest` containing fingerprints, changes, and exact approvals for table drops, column drops, and column truncations. `meta-sql deploy` checks the source and live fingerprints and applies the recorded changes.
#### Data quality
The transform estate already contains repeated joins, projections, and grain clues. `MetaDataQuality` walks that modeled structure, follows joins through CTEs and derived queries, and gathers recurring patterns across transforms. From them it produces candidates for orphan joins, outer-join null expansion, multiplicity growth, and duplicate output.
The workspace keeps each pattern, its occurrences, the generated candidates, and their promotion status. Promoted candidates become SQL views, a review dashboard, and an operational run and findings pack.
#### Pipelines
Bound transforms become runnable work in `MetaPipeline`. A pipeline arranges transform tasks and executable tasks into an ordered unit, with connection references, target writes, timeouts, and execution settings recorded in the workspace. During a run, the pipeline runtime reads and writes data, buffers batches, invokes processes, and records task results, row and batch counts, timings, metrics, and failures.
#### Orchestration
The reads and writes captured by binding give `MetaOrchestration` the information needed to connect pipeline tasks. It derives producer-consumer dependencies and object effects, then combines them with ordering, locking, retry, and failure-branch policy in an orchestration workspace.
Run planning turns that workspace into planned tasks and locks. At execution time, orchestration grants work as dependencies become satisfied and locks become available, allowing independent paths to run together while recording attempts, retries, and failure paths.
#### Analytics
At the analytical layer, `MetaAnalytics` carries tables, attributes, relationships, hierarchies, perspectives, security, cultures, translations, and source-backed base measures with typed aggregate functions. That workspace can be converted into either analytical target.
`MetaTabular` adds the Tabular structures used for DAX measures, row filters, partitions, calculation groups, roles, perspectives, and translations. `MetaMultiDimensional` carries cubes, dimensions, measure groups, MDX calculations, named sets, actions, partitions, roles, perspectives, and translations. Their CLIs deploy the target databases, process them, query them, back them up, restore them, and remove them.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: The models

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
`IMetaSchemaDiscoveryAdapter` receives a provider-resolved connection reference and a system name, then returns a `MetaSchemaModel`. The provider describes the schemas, objects, fields, keys, and relationships available from that system using the normal MetaSchema contract. `MetaSchemaAdapterWorkspaceService` writes that model as an ordinary XML, C#, or SQL workspace through the normal workspace mapper.
Binding follows the existing meta-bi path. `TransformBindingWorkspaceService` binds a MetaTransformScript workspace against the discovered source and target MetaSchema workspaces and creates a validated MetaTransformBinding workspace. No adapter-specific binding path is introduced.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Discovery and binding

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
`MetaSchemaAdapterExecutionService` loads the selected MetaSchema, MetaTransformScript, and MetaTransformBinding workspaces and uses MetaPipeline's existing execution resolver. For a row-producing transform it obtains an `IPipelineRowStreamSource` from `IMetaSchemaTransformAdapter` and an `IPipelineTargetWriteOperation` from `IMetaSchemaTargetWriteAdapter`. MetaPipeline checks the row shape, moves rows in batches, reports progress, and records the execution result. The execution service disposes the provider-owned target operation after the run.
For a mutating transform, the same service supplies the modeled contracts and selected identities to `IMetaSchemaMutationAdapter` and returns the provider's affected-row evidence.
Connection references are names resolved by the provider. Provider configuration, credentials, authentication, and physical I/O stay with the provider implementation.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Pipeline execution

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
A provider references `MetaSchema.Adapter`, implements `IMetaSchemaAdapter`, and adds only the capability interfaces it supports. Implementations translate the supported semantic forms using the transform model and binding evidence and report unsupported forms clearly. The application supplies configured adapter instances; provider package loading is left to the application host.
The meta-bi repository includes a test provider for tab-separated files in [`MetaSchemaAdapter/Tests/ExternalProvider`](https://github.com/jimmy-zhao-tainio/meta-bi/tree/main/MetaSchemaAdapter/Tests/ExternalProvider). Its integration test creates a MetaSchema workspace, imports a MetaTransformScript workspace, creates a validated MetaTransformBinding workspace through the existing binding service, evaluates the supported projection and predicate entities, and writes the result through MetaPipeline. The provider lives outside the MetaSchemaAdapter namespace and requires no changes to MetaSchema, MetaTransformBinding, or MetaPipeline.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Implementing a provider

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
`MetaSchemaAdapter` is the provider boundary for systems outside the built-in SQL Server path. It lets a provider describe an external system as MetaSchema and supply the runtime capabilities it supports for bound transforms and pipeline writes.
The contract is split by capability. A read-only provider can offer discovery and row-producing transforms, while another provider may also support mutations or target inserts.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: MetaSchemaAdapter

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
`IMetaSchemaTransformAdapter` creates an `IPipelineRowStreamSource` for a row-producing transform. `IMetaSchemaMutationAdapter` executes a bound mutating transform and returns the affected row count when the provider can report it.
The provider receives the MetaTransformScript semantic model together with the validated binding workspace and the identities of the selected transform and binding. The binding supplies resolved table sources, column references, rowsets, target evidence, and output shape. The provider works from those modeled entities rather than recovering meaning from emitted SQL text. Each provider implements the semantic forms its external system can execute.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Bound transforms

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
`meta-bi` brings BI engineering into the workspace system provided by `meta`. A project can move from a discovered source schema to Data Vault and dimensional models, bind SQL transforms to those structures, turn transform patterns into data-quality checks, execute loads, derive orchestration, and publish analytical models.
Each stage leaves a model workspace behind. Those workspaces carry the structures and decisions used by the next stage, while the command-line tools create and operate them.

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
`meta` organizes commands by the work performed on a workspace:
- **Create:** create an empty workspace or project an existing workspace onto another surface. - **Inspect:** view workspace status, models, instances, relationships, queries, and graphs. - **Author:** add or change model definitions and instance records. - **Refactor:** change model structure together with the affected instance data. - **Import and export:** bring external metadata into a workspace or write it in another supported form.
Workspace-oriented commands use the current directory by default. Pass `--workspace <path>` to target another workspace. Use `meta help` for the command list and `meta help <command>` for the current arguments and options; the complete command reference is generated from that same modeled command surface.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Meta CLI at a glance

DocumentationNarrative.Body: - [Meta CLI reference](https://metametabi.com/docs.html#group-public-meta-cli) is generated from the modeled command surfaces. - [Meta model reference](https://metametabi.com/docs.html#group-public-meta-models) describes the foundation models. - [Development package documentation](https://github.com/jimmy-zhao-tainio/meta/blob/master/PACKAGE-README.md) records the maintained package boundaries. - [Contributor guidance](https://github.com/jimmy-zhao-tainio/meta/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) covers repository builds and generated-artifact policy.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Further reference

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Create an XML workspace and give its initial model one entity and two records:
```powershell meta create --new-workspace .\XmlWorkspace --xml meta model rename-model MetadataModel WorkspaceCatalog --workspace .\XmlWorkspace meta model add-entity System --workspace .\XmlWorkspace meta model add-property System SystemName --workspace .\XmlWorkspace meta insert System erp --set SystemName=ERP --workspace .\XmlWorkspace meta insert System crm --set SystemName=CRM --workspace .\XmlWorkspace ```
Now create SQL and C# workspaces from that exact model and instance graph:
```powershell $env:META_SQL_CONNECTION = "Server=.;Database=WorkspaceCatalog;Integrated Security=true;TrustServerCertificate=true;Encrypt=false" meta create --new-workspace .\SqlWorkspace --source-workspace .\XmlWorkspace --with-instances --connection-env META_SQL_CONNECTION --sql meta create --new-workspace .\CSharpWorkspace --source-workspace .\XmlWorkspace --with-instances --csharp ```
The C# surface contains the generated `WorkspaceCatalogModel`, the `System` type, and the same two records. Application or service code can consume them directly:
```csharp using WorkspaceCatalog;
WorkspaceCatalogModel catalog = WorkspaceCatalogInstance.BuiltIn; foreach (var system in catalog.SystemList) { Console.WriteLine($"{system.Id}: {system.SystemName}"); } ```
All three workspaces carry the `WorkspaceCatalog` model, its `System` entity, and the `erp` and `crm` instances. Only their storage and execution surfaces differ.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: One workspace across XML, SQL and C#

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Metadata is the structure that tools operate on. A model defines entity types, scalar properties, and relationships. Its instance graph contains identified records and references. A workspace carries both so the same declared meaning can be authored, inspected, changed, and moved between surfaces.
Core terms:
- **Model:** a named set of entity definitions. - **Entity:** a record type with an identity. - **Property:** a scalar value on an entity. - **Relationship:** a reference from one entity to another. - **Instance:** one identified record of an entity. - **Workspace:** the unit that carries a model, its instance graph, and the selected surface.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Metadata foundations

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
The repository targets .NET 8. Build the foundation from its root:
```powershell dotnet build Metadata.Framework.sln ```
Run the CLI directly during development:
```powershell dotnet run --project Meta\Cli\Meta.Cli.csproj -- help ```
For an offline release, extract the archive without changing its layout and run `install-meta.exe`. A framework-dependent package requires the .NET 8 runtime; a self-contained package carries its runtime. The installer places `meta.exe`, `meta-weave.exe`, and `meta-docs.exe` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\meta\bin` and adds that directory to the user `PATH`. Open a new terminal, then run `meta help`.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Install and run

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
A supported surface is isomorphic when it can carry the modeled facts of a workspace without assigning them a different meaning. The model, identities, scalar values, and relationships remain the same when the workspace moves between XML, SQL, and C#.
- **XML** stores deterministic model and instance files. Their structured, stable ordering makes metadata changes practical to review, branch, merge, and version in Git. - **SQL** stores the workspace in relational tables, where database constraints, queries, and set-based operations can work over large instance sets. - **C#** stores readable and writable typed source for applications and services that need to consume or produce the workspace directly.
Commands open the selected surface through the common workspace contract, apply operations to the same modeled state, and persist through that surface or a selected destination surface. XML is not a canonical semantic form; it is one first-class representation alongside SQL and C#.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Why isomorphic metadata

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Five command-line tools share the foundation:
- **`meta`** creates and operates on model and instance workspaces across XML, SQL, and C# surfaces. - **`meta-cli`** defines modeled command surfaces and provides shared parsing, help, workspace access, and runtime binding. - **`meta-weave`** authors first-class correspondences between workspace contracts. Its WeaveScript language is modeled transformation of models, distilled from MetaTransformScript; the T-SQL-shaped text is a readable projection of semantic query graphs stored in the correspondence workspace. - **`meta-docs`** combines CLI and model reference data with authored technical documentation, then merges and renders the public reference. - **`meta-mesh`** declares the workspaces involved in a repository workflow and the ordered executable steps that operate on them.
BI-specific models and command-line tools live in the separate `meta-bi` repository.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Foundation command-line tools

DocumentationNarrative.Body: `meta` is a model-first metadata foundation. It lets tools and people create, inspect, change, and move one workspace contract across XML, SQL, and C# without making any one representation the source of semantic truth.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Overview

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
A workspace contains one model, one instance graph, and the storage required by its selected surface. Commands address the workspace as a unit rather than depending on a particular file, table, or generated type.
The line-oriented `workspace.meta` descriptor selects the surface with `representation xml`, `representation sql`, or `representation csharp`. A SQL workspace also names the environment variable that supplies its database connection. XML files, SQL tables, and C# source remain owned by their respective surfaces behind this common boundary.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Workspace contract
